- backwpup-architecture: Use this skill when changing service structure, shared logic, bootstrapping, dependency wiring, or any code that may affect FREE/PRO boundaries in BackWPup.
- backwpup-frontend-architecture: Use this skill when changing admin JavaScript, CSS, or HTML templates in BackWPUp Pro.
- sprint-shortlister: Generate a sprint shortlist for wp-media/backwpup-pro with fast story point estimation and capacity planning.

Use this skill whenever you need to:
- Plan a 2-week sprint for BackWPUp Pro with realistic team capacity constraints
- Quickly estimate effort on unstarted issues without full grooming analysis
- Create a balanced shortlist across bugs, features, and tech debt
- Generate a shareable HTML report for sprint planning meetings

The skill asks for team size (default: 2 developers), optionally a target milestone, then fetches open unassigned issues from the repo. It estimates story points through lightweight scope analysis, builds a prioritized shortlist to fit the sprint capacity, and outputs an interactive HTML report ready to share with stakeholders. The entire process takes 2–3 minutes.
- changelog: Generate a changelog entry from merged PRs since the last git tag. Use this when preparing a release, drafting release notes, or summarizing what changed between versions — even if the user says "what changed since last release" or "help me write release notes". Invoke with `/changelog` (since last tag) or `/changelog v3.x.x` (since a specific tag).
- checkout: List all your unread GitHub notifications, grouped by priority and type (mention, review requested, assigned, etc.) with clickable URLs. Use this as a quick daily triage of everything waiting for your attention on GitHub — like checking github.com/notifications but from the terminal. Invoke with `/checkout`.
- estimate: Estimate the complexity of a GitHub issue for sprint planning. Use this whenever someone wants to size a ticket, groom a backlog item, plan a sprint, or get a sense of effort — even if they just say "how big is this?" or "is this a quick fix?". Invoke with `/estimate <issue-number>` or `/estimate <GitHub issue URL>`.
- skill-audit: Audit all Claude skill files for stale references, ambiguous triggers, and hardcoded values. Use this periodically to keep the skill library healthy — invoke with `/skill-audit`. Reports PASS / WARN / FAIL per skill. Does NOT auto-fix anything.
- standup: Generate a standup update from yesterday's git activity and PR status. Use this whenever you need to prepare a standup message, daily update, or summary of recent work — even if the user just says "what did I do yesterday" or "help me write my standup". Invoke with `/standup` (for yesterday) or `/standup YYYY-MM-DD` (for a specific date).
- standup-global: Generate a standup update from your GitHub activity across ALL repositories — not just the current project. Use this instead of /standup when you work across multiple repos and want a full picture of yesterday's work. Invoke with `/standup-global` (for yesterday) or `/standup-global YYYY-MM-DD` (for a specific date).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- maestro:docs: Update developer-facing documentation to reflect code changes on the current branch. Runs as an inline skill inside backend-agent and frontend-agent (step 2.5 of the internal sequence) after implementation and before DOD. Receives the explicit list of changed files from the implementation agent. No-op if no public API changes occurred.
- maestro:dod
- maestro:e2e
- maestro:issue-workflow
- maestro:knowledge-graph
- maestro:orchestrator
- maestro:wordpress-compliance
- agents-observe:observe: Agents Observe dashboard and server management
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boot the wp-env Docker environment and activate the plugin.
# Idempotent — safe to run if the environment is already running.
set -euo pipefail

SEED="${1:-}"

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "Starting wp-env..."
npx @wordpress/env start

echo "Activating plugin..."
npx @wordpress/env run cli wp plugin activate backwpup-pro

if [[ "$SEED" != "--no-seed" ]]; then
  bash bin/dev-seed.sh
fi

echo "Done. WordPress is available at http://localhost:8888"
echo "Admin: http://localhost:8888/wp-admin  (admin / password)"
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop the wp-env Docker environment.
# Pass --destroy to also remove volumes and the database.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--destroy" ]]; then
  echo "Destroying wp-env (volumes and DB will be removed)..."
  npx @wordpress/env destroy --yes
else
  echo "Stopping wp-env..."
  npx @wordpress/env stop
fi
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Seed the wp-env environment with test data for E2E tests.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

WP="npx @wordpress/env run cli wp"

echo "Seeding test data..."

# Set a dummy license key if provided via env var (enables PRO features).
if [[ -n "${BACKWPUP_TESTS_LICENSE_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  $WP eval "
    \$options = get_option( 'backwpup', [] );
    \$options['license_key'] = '${BACKWPUP_TESTS_LICENSE_KEY}';
    update_option( 'backwpup', \$options );
  "
  echo "  License key set."
fi

# Create a seed backup job (DB-only, local folder) if none exists.
$WP eval '
  foreach ( BackWPup_Option::get_job_ids() as $job_id ) {
      if ( "BackWPup E2E Seed Job" === BackWPup_Option::get( $job_id, "name" ) ) {
          echo "seed-job-exists:" . $job_id;
          return;
      }
  }
  $job_id = BackWPup_Option::create_default_jobs( "BackWPup E2E Seed Job", [ "DBDUMP" ] );
  BackWPup_Option::update( $job_id, "backupdir", WP_CONTENT_DIR . "/uploads/backwpup-e2e-tests/" );
  BackWPup_Option::update( $job_id, "cronselect", "manuell" );
  echo "seed-job-created:" . $job_id;
'

# Mark onboarding as complete so other admin pages don't redirect to onboarding.
$WP eval "delete_site_option( 'backwpup_onboarding' );"

echo "Done seeding."
